title: The Gulper at the Gate
story: The salt caravan has gone three days without water, and the stone gate to the oasis only swings open when the basin holds 90 gallons. Quaffalon, a bloated sand-frog the size of a haycart, has parked himself in the basin and slurps away at it all day long. Mr 6 wedges his little shield under the gulper's chin so the slurping slows to a steady trickle, then sits down with a stick to do sums in the sand.
question: The spring pours 11.5 gallons into the basin each minute while Quaffalon slurps out 7 gallons each minute. The basin holds 18 gallons right now and the gate opens at 90 gallons. How many minutes until the gate opens?
solution: Each minute the basin really gains 11.5 - 7 = 4.5 gallons.
72 / 4.5 = 16 minutes until the gate swings open.
praise: Looking at both the pouring and the slurping was exactly right — the missing step was turning those two numbers into one net gain per minute.
hint: Water is coming in AND going out. Work out how much the basin truly gains in one single minute before you worry about the total.
victory: At minute sixteen the gate groaned open, and Quaffalon — now sloshing like a full waterskin — burped once and hopped off to nap in the shade. The camels drank first; Mr 6 drank second, as knights should.
imagePrompt: A brave number-six knight with a blue cape crouching beside a desert oasis basin at golden dusk, scratching sums in the sand while an enormous bloated sand-frog slurps noisily from the water behind a half-open stone gate.
